title: Tummly
description: Tummly is a restaurant-management SaaS product designed around restaurant onboarding, account management, and restaurant / group / location structures. I worked on the application as a full-stack engineer with responsibility across the frontend and backend.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.text: A React frontend consumes a REST API served by an ASP.NET Core / C# backend, backed by SQL Server. Onboarding runs as a linear workflow — trial request, OTP/email verification, admin review, approval or decline, then a secure registration link that provisions the account and its restaurant / group / location structure.

sections.heading: Scope & engineering focus
items: OTP / email verification and admin approval workflow
Single-account and multi-account onboarding paths
Restaurant, group and location management
Secure registration links generated after admin approval
Pixel-accurate Figma-to-code frontend implementation

sections.heading: Key engineering decisions
items: Kept onboarding as an explicit, auditable state machine (requested → verified → reviewed → approved) rather than a single form submission
Separated restaurant, group and location as distinct entities to support both single-location and multi-location operators

sections.heading: Challenges
items: Coordinating an admin-approval step with time-sensitive OTP verification without creating a confusing wait state for applicants
Translating Figma layouts into responsive, pixel-accurate React components across the onboarding and dashboard flows

title: EventSphere
description: EventSphere is a full-stack event / expo management platform designed around multiple user roles and real operational workflows: organizers running expos, exhibitors applying and managing booths, and attendees registering and engaging with sessions.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.text: A Vite-built React frontend talks to an Express REST API backed by MongoDB. Collections include users, expos, booths, exhibitor applications and profiles, sessions, registrations, bookmarks, messages, notifications, feedback and analytics events, with compound indexes supporting the role-based query patterns.

sections.heading: Scope & engineering focus
items: Role-based access control across organizer, exhibitor and attendee roles
Expo lifecycle management: draft → published → ongoing → completed, with cancellation support
Exhibitor applications, booth management and session participation
Attendee registration, bookmarks, messaging and notifications
Mongoose schemas with validation, unique constraints and compound indexes

sections.heading: Key engineering decisions
items: Modeled the expo lifecycle as an explicit status field with guarded transitions instead of inferring state from related records
Used JWT-based route protection per role rather than a single shared permission flag

sections.heading: Challenges
items: Designing a schema that cleanly supports three different user roles interacting with the same expo and booth records
Keeping notification and messaging logic consistent as new event types and statuses were added

title: StreamScale
description: StreamScale is a system-design-heavy project exploring a video streaming platform's backend architecture: an API gateway in front of independent services, event-driven communication through Kafka, caching through Redis, and observability through Prometheus and Grafana.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.text: Client requests pass through Nginx to an API gateway, which routes to purpose-built microservices (auth, catalog, analytics, recommendation). Services communicate asynchronously through Kafka where appropriate, share a Redis cache, and persist to MongoDB. Background workers handle media-processing workflows. Prometheus scrapes service metrics; Grafana visualizes them.

sections.heading: Scope & engineering focus
items: Nginx-fronted API gateway routing to independent microservices
Authentication, catalog, analytics and recommendation services
Kafka-driven event processing and background workers for media/transcoding workflows
Redis caching layer for frequently accessed catalog data
Prometheus metrics collection with Grafana dashboards

sections.heading: Key engineering decisions
items: Chose an event-driven pattern over direct service-to-service calls for workflows that don't need a synchronous response
Kept metrics and dashboards as a first-class part of the architecture rather than an afterthought

sections.heading: Challenges
items: Reasoning about eventual consistency across services that both read and write catalog data
Structuring Docker Compose so the gateway, services, Kafka/Zookeeper and observability stack start up in a workable order

title: Verendo
description: Verendo is a production-oriented full-stack application built to practice and demonstrate clean architecture on the MERN stack — authentication, validated APIs, structured error handling and a deployment-ready client/server split, rather than a single-file tutorial-style build.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.text: A React/Vite client consumes a versioned Express REST API. Mongoose models enforce schema-level validation; middleware handles authentication, error formatting and request logging. Configuration is environment-driven so the same codebase runs locally and in a deployed environment without code changes.

sections.heading: Scope & engineering focus
items: JWT-based authentication and route-protection middleware
Request validation and structured, consistent error handling
Environment-based configuration for local vs. deployed environments
Clear separation between the API and the client application

sections.heading: Key engineering decisions
items: Centralized error handling in Express middleware instead of repeating try/catch formatting in every route
Kept the API versioned and client-agnostic so it isn't tightly coupled to any one frontend

sections.heading: Challenges
items: Keeping validation logic consistent between the client form layer and the API layer
Structuring middleware order correctly so authentication, validation and error handling compose cleanly

title: Usama AI
description: Usama AI is an AI engineering project: a full-stack chat application that orchestrates a language model, streams its response back to the client, and augments answers with live web search for questions that need current information.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.text: The React client sends a question to an Express API, which calls a web-search provider when the query needs current context, assembles a prompt, and streams the model's response back to the client over Server-Sent Events as it's generated. All provider API keys stay server-side.

sections.heading: Scope & engineering focus
items: Streaming AI responses to the client over Server-Sent Events
Web-search-augmented answers for queries needing current information
Server-side API key and secret management (keys never reach the client)
React chat interface with incremental message rendering

sections.heading: Key engineering decisions
items: Used Server-Sent Events rather than polling so responses render incrementally as the model generates them
Ran web search as a conditional pre-step rather than on every request, to keep simple questions fast

sections.heading: Challenges
items: Handling partial/interrupted streams gracefully on the client without corrupting the rendered message
Deciding when a query actually needs a web-search pass versus when the model can answer directly

title: Nexora
description: Nexora is a flagship Flutter/Dart project: a business-operations mobile platform concept connected to a REST backend, covering authentication, dashboards, task and project views, and notifications, structured with a clean, testable architecture.

sections.heading: Architecture
sections.text: The UI layer talks to Provider-based state management, which delegates to a repository layer, which in turn calls an API service layer over REST. Folder structure separates core/config, models, services, repositories, providers, screens, widgets, routes and utils, keeping network and presentation concerns independent.

sections.heading: Scope & engineering focus
items: Token-managed authentication state with secure local storage
Repository-pattern API abstraction between screens and network calls
Loading, empty and error states handled consistently across screens
Theme system with dark mode support

sections.heading: Key engineering decisions
items: Used the repository pattern so screens never call the network layer directly, keeping API changes isolated
Treated loading / empty / error as first-class UI states for every screen rather than an afterthought

sections.heading: Challenges
items: Keeping token refresh and auth state consistent across a multi-screen navigation stack
Designing a folder architecture that stays legible as more feature screens are added
